segments.heading: Why now
segments.narration: The holidays are when money slips. A challenge with one small move a week is easier to stick to than a big goal you forget by Thursday.

segments.narration: Eight moves, one every Sunday. A cart pause on Black Friday week. One subscription and one thing you sell. A pantry week. One bill call. A gift cap. Returns and gift cards. Then a final round-up on New Year's Eve.

segments.narration: The amounts are an example plan: twenty, forty, fifty, forty-five, thirty-five, forty, fifty and twenty. That adds up to three hundred. Your numbers will be different, and that's fine.

segments.heading: The move
segments.narration: Pick one thing in a cart this week that you want but didn't plan. Leave it there for seventy-two hours. Set a reminder.

segments.heading: Why it works
segments.narration: Sales are built for fast decisions: countdown timers, low-stock warnings. Waiting three days takes the urgency out, and a lot of carts look different by Monday.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a countdown timer with a pause button. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Move the money
segments.narration: If you skip it, move what it would have cost into your bucket. Our example: a forty-dollar item. If you still want it after three days, and it fits your budget, that's fine too.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a coin moving from a cart to a jar. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Not a no
segments.narration: This isn't a rule against buying. It's a pause. If it's something you'd been planning to buy anyway, and the price is genuinely lower, buying it on sale is a good move. The pause is for the impulse buys.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a pause button over a gift box. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Part 1
segments.narration: Part one: open your bank app and search the last two months for repeating charges. Find one you haven't used in a month and cancel it. Our example: fifteen dollars.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a bank statement with one line circled. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Tip
segments.narration: Can't decide? Pause instead of cancelling, if the service allows it. And check for free trials that turn into paid plans in December.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a pause button and a calendar. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Part 2
segments.narration: Part two: sell one thing you don't use. Good bets this time of year are kids' gear, small furniture, tools and unused gifts from last year. Our example: thirty-five dollars.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a chair with a price tag. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Selling safely
segments.narration: Selling locally? Meet in a public place in daylight, bring someone if you can, and take payment before handing anything over. Clean photos in natural light sell faster.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a small shield next to a box. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The move
segments.narration: Before you shop this week, look in the freezer, the fridge and the cupboard. Plan five dinners around what's there, and buy only the gaps, like milk, fruit or one fresh vegetable.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a short list next to a freezer. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Ideas
segments.narration: Easy pantry dinners: pasta with tinned tomatoes, fried rice with frozen veg, bean chilli, soup, eggs on toast. Nothing fancy, and that's the point.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a pot, a pan and a bowl. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The math
segments.narration: Compare this week's grocery bill with a normal week. Our example: a normal week is one hundred twenty, pantry week is seventy-five. The forty-five dollar difference goes in the bucket.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. two receipts side by side. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Leftovers
segments.narration: Cook a little extra on two of the nights, and lunch is covered the next day too. That's often where the biggest grocery savings hide, because lunches out add up quickly over a week.

segments.heading: Pick one
segments.narration: Pick your biggest bill that has competitors: internet, mobile phone or car insurance. Look up what new customers are offered, for you and from a competitor.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. three small icons in a row. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The script
segments.narration: Then call and say: I've been a customer for a while, and I've seen offers around this price. I'd like to stay, but I need a better rate. What can you do? If they can't help, ask for the retention team.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a phone with a speech bubble. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The math
segments.narration: Our example: the internet bill drops from eighty-five to fifty-five, a thirty-dollar saving each month. Move this month's thirty, plus five you skipped on takeout this week.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. a bill with a lower number. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: In writing
segments.narration: Whatever they offer, ask how long the price lasts and what it goes to afterwards. Ask them to confirm it by email or in the app.
segments.visual_prompt: Warm flat vector illustration, muted greens and cream with a mustard accent, simple shapes. an email icon with a tick. No text, no logos, no real people.
